title: New Breakthrough Drug Offers Hope for Pancreatic Cancer Patients
subtitle: The FDA has approved a new treatment that targets a protein long thought to be impossible to reach.

summary.en: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved a new drug called daraxonrasib for patients with pancreatic cancer. This daily pill targets a specific protein that helps tumors grow, which was previously considered impossible to treat. Clinical trials showed that the drug nearly doubled the survival time for patients compared to traditional chemotherapy. While the drug can cause side effects like skin rashes, it is seen as a major step forward in fighting this deadly disease. Experts hope this approval will lead to more effective treatment options in the future.
summary.zh: 美國食品藥物管理局已核准一款名為 daraxonrasib 的新藥，用於治療胰臟癌病患。這款每日服用的藥丸能針對一種有助於腫瘤生長的特定蛋白質，而該蛋白質過去被認為無法透過藥物治療。臨床試驗顯示，與傳統化學治療相比，該藥物幾乎將病患的存活時間延長了一倍。雖然該藥物可能引起皮膚紅疹等副作用，但它被視為對抗此致命疾病的一大進展。專家希望此次核准能引領未來出現更多有效的治療選擇。

paragraphs.en: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has officially approved a new, groundbreaking drug for the most common form of pancreatic cancer. This decision provides a new and more effective treatment option for patients facing one of the deadliest types of cancer. The new pill, known by its medical name daraxonrasib and sold under the brand name Rasonque, is the first of its kind to successfully block a mutated protein that fuels tumor growth. This protein is present in more than 90% of pancreatic cancer cases, a target that scientists have struggled to reach for many decades.
paragraphs.zh: 美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）已正式核准一款針對最常見胰臟癌類型的突破性新藥。這項決策為面對此類致命癌症的病患，提供了一種嶄新且更有效的治療選擇。這款新藥的醫學名稱為 daraxonrasib，商品名為 Rasonque，是首款能成功阻斷助長腫瘤生長之突變蛋白質的藥物。這種蛋白質存在於超過百分之九十的胰臟癌病例中，是科學家數十年來難以攻克的目標。

paragraphs.en: Pancreatic cancer is widely considered one of the most difficult diseases to treat. This is largely because it is very hard to detect before it begins to spread to other organs. According to The Guardian Health, the American Cancer Society estimates that about 67,000 new cases will be diagnosed in the United States this year, with more than 52,000 people expected to die from the disease. The five-year survival rate remains low at 13%, making any new development in treatment highly significant for both doctors and patients.
paragraphs.zh: 胰臟癌被廣泛認為是最難治療的疾病之一，主要原因在於它在擴散至其他器官前極難被偵測。根據《衛報健康版》（The Guardian Health）報導，美國癌症協會估計今年美國將新增約六萬七千名病例，預計有超過五萬兩千人會死於此病。胰臟癌的五年存活率僅維持在百分之十三的低點，因此任何治療上的新進展，對醫師與病患而言都意義重大。

paragraphs.en: The approval follows a study called the RASolute 302 trial, which included 500 patients whose cancer had already spread and stopped responding to earlier treatments. MedPage Today reports that patients who took the new drug lived for a median of 13.2 months, compared to only 6.7 months for those who received standard chemotherapy. This means the drug effectively doubled the survival time for patients in the study. Additionally, the drug showed a significant improvement in progression-free survival, which measures how long a patient lives without their cancer getting worse.
paragraphs.zh: 此次核准是基於一項名為 RASolute 302 的臨床試驗，該試驗納入了五百名癌症已擴散且對先前治療不再產生反應的病患。根據《MedPage Today》報導，服用新藥的病患存活期中位數為十三點二個月，而接受標準化學治療的病患僅有六點七個月。這意味著該藥物有效地將試驗中病患的存活時間延長了一倍。此外，該藥物在「無惡化存活期」（衡量病患在癌症未惡化情況下存活時間的指標）方面也展現了顯著的改善。

paragraphs.en: For a long time, the specific protein targeted by this drug was considered "undruggable" because its structure made it very difficult for medicines to attach to it. However, the manufacturer, Revolution Medicines, developed a technology that acts like a molecular glue to bind with multiple forms of this protein. Dr. Rachna Shroff of the University of Arizona Cancer Center noted that these results provide proof that targeting this specific pathway is critical for treating pancreatic cancer. At a recent medical meeting, Dr. Julie Gralow of the American Society of Clinical Oncology described the study results as a “grand slam” for cancer research.
paragraphs.zh: 長期以來，該藥物所針對的特定蛋白質被視為「無法藥物化」，因為其結構使得藥物難以與其結合。然而，製造商 Revolution Medicines 開發了一種技術，能像分子膠水一樣與該蛋白質的多種形式結合。亞利桑那大學癌症中心（University of Arizona Cancer Center）的拉赫娜·史洛夫（Rachna Shroff）醫師指出，這些結果證明針對此特定路徑是治療胰臟癌的關鍵。在近期的一場醫學會議上，美國臨床腫瘤學會（American Society of Clinical Oncology）的茱莉·葛拉洛（Julie Gralow）醫師形容此試驗結果是癌症研究的一記「全壘打」。

paragraphs.en: The drug gained public attention earlier this year when former US senator Ben Sasse shared his personal experience, noting that he felt less pain while taking it. This public interest led the FDA to allow “expanded access”—a program that lets patients get a new medicine before it is fully approved if they meet certain requirements. The FDA ultimately approved the drug more than six months ahead of their original deadline. Kyle Diamantas, the FDA’s acting commissioner, stated that it is their duty to deliver meaningful treatments to patients as quickly as possible.
paragraphs.zh: 該藥物於今年稍早因前美國參議員班·薩斯（Ben Sasse）分享其個人用藥經驗，提到服用後疼痛感減輕，因而受到大眾關注。這股公眾興趣促使 FDA 允許「擴大使用」（expanded access）——這是一項讓病患在符合特定條件下，能在藥物正式獲准前取得新藥的計畫。FDA 最終比原定截止日期提前了超過六個月核准該藥。FDA 代理局長凱爾·迪亞曼塔斯（Kyle Diamantas）表示，盡快為病患提供有意義的治療是他們的職責。

paragraphs.en: While the results are promising, the drug does have side effects. MedPage Today reports that the most common issue for patients was a skin rash, which affected over 85% of those taking the medication. Other serious side effects included mouth sores, known as stomatitis. However, the study found that patients were much less likely to stop taking the new drug due to side effects compared to those receiving traditional chemotherapy.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管結果令人振奮，該藥物仍有副作用。《MedPage Today》報導指出，病患最常見的問題是皮膚紅疹，影響了超過百分之八十五的用藥者。其他嚴重副作用包括口腔潰瘍，即口炎。然而，研究發現與接受傳統化學治療的病患相比，因副作用而停止服用新藥的病患比例顯著較低。

paragraphs.en: Doctors who specialize in treating pancreatic cancer are feeling optimistic about the future. Unlike other types of cancer that have many different treatment options, pancreatic cancer has historically been very difficult to tackle. Experts hope that the success of this drug will encourage the development of other new treatments. Revolution Medicines is already studying whether this technology could be used to treat other types of cancer, such as lung cancer. For now, the medical community views this approval as a major shift in the standard of care for patients who have already tried other treatments without success.
paragraphs.zh: 專精於胰臟癌治療的醫師們對未來感到樂觀。與其他擁有眾多治療選擇的癌症不同，胰臟癌在歷史上一直非常難以處理。專家希望此藥的成功將能鼓勵其他新療法的開發。Revolution Medicines 已經在研究該技術是否能用於治療其他類型的癌症，例如肺癌。目前，醫學界將此次核准視為針對已嘗試過其他治療卻無效的病患，在照護標準上的一大轉變。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To stop something from moving, growing, or working.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（街區、積木），這裡作動詞用。文中：is the first of its kind to successfully block a mutated protein that fuels tumor growth.
原指體育賽事中的大滿貫，這裡比喻研究成果非常成功。文中：Dr. Julie Gralow of the American Society of Clinical Oncology described the study results as a “grand slam” for cancer research.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To deal with or try to solve a difficult problem.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於運動（擒抱），這裡指處理棘手的疾病。文中：pancreatic cancer has historically been very difficult to tackle.

quiz.question: According to the RASolute 302 trial, how did the survival outcomes of patients taking Rasonque compare to those receiving standard chemotherapy?

options.A: They lived for a median of 6.7 months longer than those on chemotherapy.
options.B: They experienced a median survival time that was twice as long as the chemotherapy group.
options.C: They showed a 13% increase in their five-year survival rate compared to the control group.
options.D: They were 85% more likely to survive without their cancer progressing.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第三段明確指出，服用新藥的患者存活期中位數為 13.2 個月，而標準化療組僅為 6.7 個月，這意味著存活時間增加了一倍。選項 A 錯誤，因為 6.7 個月是化療組的存活期，而非增加的時長。選項 C 混淆了文章提到的整體五年存活率（13%）與試驗結果。選項 D 的 85% 是指皮膚紅疹的副作用比例，而非存活率數據。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the 'undruggable' nature of the protein targeted by Rasonque?

options.A: The protein is impossible to detect in most pancreatic cancer patients.
options.B: Previous medications were ineffective because they could not physically connect to the protein's structure.
options.C: The protein only exists in patients whose cancer has already spread to other organs.
options.D: Scientists have only recently discovered that this protein fuels tumor growth.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。第四段提到該蛋白質長期被認為「無法藥物治療」（undruggable），原因是其結構使得藥物難以附著（attach），而新藥透過分子膠技術解決了此問題，故可推斷過去藥物失效與結構附著困難有關。選項 A 與文意相反，該蛋白存在於 90% 的病例中。選項 C 無法從文中推論，文中僅提到該蛋白在多種癌症中存在。選項 D 錯誤，文中提到科學家已研究此目標數十年。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does Dr. Julie Gralow mean when she describes the study results as a 'grand slam'?

options.A: The results were a complete and significant success.
options.B: The study was conducted in a very aggressive manner.
options.C: The research faced many unexpected obstacles.
options.D: The findings were primarily focused on sports-related health issues.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。「Grand slam」源自棒球術語「滿貫全壘打」，在文中用來比喻研究取得了極大的成功或突破。選項 B 錯誤，此詞並非形容研究過程的手段。選項 C 與文意完全相反，該詞代表成功而非障礙。選項 D 是字面上的誤解，該詞在此處是隱喻用法，與運動賽事無關。

quiz.question: What is the primary focus of this article?

options.A: To provide a detailed guide on how to manage the side effects of pancreatic cancer drugs.
options.B: To criticize the FDA for its slow approval process regarding new cancer treatments.
options.C: To explain the history of pancreatic cancer research over the last century.
options.D: To report on the approval and significance of a new, effective drug for pancreatic cancer.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。整篇文章的核心在於介紹 FDA 核准了一款名為 Rasonque 的新藥，並探討其臨床意義、技術突破以及對胰臟癌治療帶來的希望。選項 A 僅是文章的一小部分內容，非主旨。選項 B 與文意不符，文章提到 FDA 甚至提前核准了該藥。選項 C 錯誤，文章重點在於最新的藥物突破，而非歷史回顧。
